name: RegBase Vector Pipeline (HFusion → HIVM)
scope: The RegBase (A5-class target) vector compilation path from HFusion shape normalization through vectorization, VF-scope merging, bufferization, and stride-aligned memory preparation: the passes hfusion-flatten-ops, propagate-reshape, hfusion-auto-vectorize-v2, hfusion-merge-vf, hivm-mark-stride-align, hivm-enable-stride-align and the pipeline wiring that orders them. Excludes the individual pass internals (each has its own child dossier), the legacy AutoVectorize (V1) branch, and post-alignment lowering.

related_entities.name: OutlineVectorFunction
related_entities.relation: context-only stage immediately after AutoVectorizeV2 that materializes hivm.vector_function callees

related_entities.name: OneShotBufferize + TensorCopyInsertion
related_entities.relation: context-only stage: the tensor→memref representation boundary between the two MergeVecScope placements

related_entities.name: PreMarkStrideAlign / FoldAllocReshape
related_entities.relation: context-only stages inside alignStoragePipeline around MarkStrideAlign

related_entities.name: VFFusion
related_entities.relation: context-only upstream analysis pass producing the fusion groups AutoVectorizeV2 consumes

related_entities.name: HIVMFlattenOps
related_entities.relation: context-only: the DISTINCT HIVM-level flatten pass (hivm-flatten-ops) after buffer sizing; not the requested HFusionFlattenOps

related_entities.name: hivm::MemrefAliasAnalysisState
related_entities.relation: shared analysis state consumed by MergeVecScope (READY child bundle exists)

why_this_subject: Real user goal: explain to other compiler engineers why this chain of passes coexists, in this order, with these cross-pass contracts — why flattening precedes vectorization, why MergeVecScope has two mutually exclusive placements around bufferization, and why stride alignment is marked post-bufferization and enabled afterwards. This is the first multi-subject composition dogfood: six requested passes are composed from READY child bundles plus fresh cross-component evidence.
